summary: An 80-foot Aermotor LS40 tower built in 1935-36 by the Forest Service and a CCC crew, beside the Gum Springs Recreation Area in Kisatchie National Forest.

facts.design: 80-foot Aermotor LS40 steel-frame tower with a 7x7-foot cab

events.note: Register's Built field gives 1936; its description says built during 1935-1936 by the Forest Service and CCC Troop F-6

evidence.supports: tower beside the Gum Springs Recreation Area
evidence.quote: It is adjacent to the CCC-built Gum Springs Recreation Area

notes_for_editor: Thin on the tower itself: the register page is the only source about the tower; the 2010 NRHP nomination and the NPS page cover the recreation area and say the CCC built the tower only 'likely'. No staffing, current access or post-2011 condition was found, so access and staffing are left out of facts. The firemen's dwelling dates (1935-1958) belong to the cabin, not the tower. The register says 'CCC Troop F-6' and the NPS page says 'Company 5407, Camp F-6'; the story flags this without merging them as fact. Not used: the register gives the recreation area's NRHP listing as December 2011, while Wikipedia gives December 7, 2010 citing the NPS weekly list; this concerns the recreation area, not the tower. The nhlr.org Lookout.aspx?id=906 page returned HTTP 500. Used about 10 distinct pages, over the 6-read budget, because the tower has few sources.
